verses.1: David assembled all the leaders of Israel—chiefs of the tribes, commanders of divisions who were in attendance on the king, commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds, overseers of the king’s possessions, and the royal attendants, the warriors, and all the might of the king—to Jerusalem.
verses.2: David the king stood up and said, "Listen to me, my brothers and my people: it has been on my heart to build a house of rest for the covenant chest of the LORD and to provide a place for the feet of our God. I have prepared myself to build it.
verses.3: But God said to me, 'You will not build a house for my name, because you are a man of war and have shed blood.'
verses.4: Yet the LORD, the God of Israel, chose me from among all my father's house to be king over Israel forever. He chose Judah to be the ruler, and from the house of Judah, my father’s house, he chose me to be king over all Israel.
verses.5: From among all my sons (for the LORD has given me many sons), he has chosen Solomon my son to sit on the throne of the kingdom of the LORD over Israel.
verses.6: And he said to me, 'It is Solomon your son who will build my house and my courtyards, for I have chosen him to be my son, and I will be to him a father.
verses.7: I will establish his kingdom forever, if he is determined to carry out my commandments and my ordinances as I do today.'
verses.8: Now, in the sight of all Israel, the assembly of the LORD, and in the hearing of our God, pay attention and seek all the commandments of the LORD your God, so that you may possess the good land and leave it as an inheritance to your children forever.
verses.9: You, Solomon my son, know the God of your father and serve him with a whole heart and a willing mind, for the LORD searches every heart and understands every plan and thought. If you seek him, he will be found by you; but if you abandon him, he will abandon you forever.
verses.10: See now, the LORD has chosen you to build a house for the sanctuary. Be strong and act.
verses.11: David gave to Solomon his son the plan of the temple and its chambers, its treasuries, its upper rooms, and its inner chambers, and the chamber of atonement.
verses.12: He gave him the plan of all that was in his mind for the courtyards of the house of the LORD, for all the side rooms surrounding the storehouses of the house of God, and for the storehouses of the sacred things.
verses.13: He also gave the divisions of the priests and Levites and all the work of the service of the house of the LORD, and for all the vessels of the service of the house of the LORD.
verses.14: He gave the weight for the gold for all the service vessels, and the weight for the silver for all the service vessels.
verses.15: The weight for the golden lamps and their lampstands, each lamp and its stand in gold, and the weight for the silver lamps and their lampstands, each lamp and its stand, according to the work of the lamp and its stand.
verses.16: The weight for the golden table of the bread offering, each table and its table in gold, and the weight for the silver tables of the bread offering.
verses.17: The bowls, the basins, and the ladles in pure gold, and the weight for the gold clasps, each clasp and its clasp, and the weight for the silver clasps, each clasp and its clasp.
verses.18: For the altar of incense in refined gold, the weight for it; and for the pattern of the cherubim with their wings and their covering over the covenant chest of the LORD.
verses.19: All of these were written in the hand of the LORD and given to me so that I could understand all the works of the design.
verses.20: And David said to Solomon his son, "Be strong and courageous, and act. Do not fear or be dismayed, for the LORD, my God, is with you; he will not leave you or forsake you until all the work for the service of the house of the LORD is finished."
verses.21: And behold, the divisions of the priests and Levites are assigned to every service in the house of God, and they are with you in every work, and every willing person in wisdom for every craft, and the leaders and all the people are for all your words.

notes:
Notes
- v. 3: "You will not build a house for my name" — the Hebrew uses "לִשְׁמִי" ("for my name") in reference to the temple, a common biblical idiom for the dwelling place of God.
- v. 5: "the throne of the kingdom of the LORD" — the Hebrew is "כִּסֵּא מַלְכוּת יְהוָה," which reflects the divine kingship over Israel.
- v. 14-17: The detailed measurements and weights for the temple furnishings are translated to retain their specificity and function.
- v. 20: "Do not fear or be dismayed" — the Hebrew uses "תִּירָא" and "תֵּחָת," which are standard biblical verbs for fear and discouragement.
- v. 21: "every willing person in wisdom for every craft" — the Hebrew "לְכָל־נָדִיב בַּֽחָכְמָה" is interpreted to reflect both willing volunteers and those skilled in wisdom.
raw:
[1] David assembled all the leaders of Israel—chiefs of the tribes, commanders of divisions who were in attendance on the king, commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds, overseers of the king’s possessions, and the royal attendants, the warriors, and all the might of the king—to Jerusalem.

[2] David the king stood up and said, "Listen to me, my brothers and my people: it has been on my heart to build a house of rest for the covenant chest of the LORD and to provide a place for the feet of our God. I have prepared myself to build it.

[3] But God said to me, 'You will not build a house for my name, because you are a man of war and have shed blood.'

[4] Yet the LORD, the God of Israel, chose me from among all my father's house to be king over Israel forever. He chose Judah to be the ruler, and from the house of Judah, my father’s house, he chose me to be king over all Israel.

[5] From among all my sons (for the LORD has given me many sons), he has chosen Solomon my son to sit on the throne of the kingdom of the LORD over Israel.

[6] And he said to me, 'It is Solomon your son who will build my house and my courtyards, for I have chosen him to be my son, and I will be to him a father.

[7] I will establish his kingdom forever, if he is determined to carry out my commandments and my ordinances as I do today.'

[8] Now, in the sight of all Israel, the assembly of the LORD, and in the hearing of our God, pay attention and seek all the commandments of the LORD your God, so that you may possess the good land and leave it as an inheritance to your children forever.

[9] You, Solomon my son, know the God of your father and serve him with a whole heart and a willing mind, for the LORD searches every heart and understands every plan and thought. If you seek him, he will be found by you; but if you abandon him, he will abandon you forever.

[10] See now, the LORD has chosen you to build a house for the sanctuary. Be strong and act.

[11] David gave to Solomon his son the plan of the temple and its chambers, its treasuries, its upper rooms, and its inner chambers, and the chamber of atonement.

[12] He gave him the plan of all that was in his mind for the courtyards of the house of the LORD, for all the side rooms surrounding the storehouses of the house of God, and for the storehouses of the sacred things.

[13] He also gave the divisions of the priests and Levites and all the work of the service of the house of the LORD, and for all the vessels of the service of the house of the LORD.

[14] He gave the weight for the gold for all the service vessels, and the weight for the silver for all the service vessels.

[15] The weight for the golden lamps and their lampstands, each lamp and its stand in gold, and the weight for the silver lamps and their lampstands, each lamp and its stand, according to the work of the lamp and its stand.

[16] The weight for the golden table of the bread offering, each table and its table in gold, and the weight for the silver tables of the bread offering.

[17] The bowls, the basins, and the ladles in pure gold, and the weight for the gold clasps, each clasp and its clasp, and the weight for the silver clasps, each clasp and its clasp.

[18] For the altar of incense in refined gold, the weight for it; and for the pattern of the cherubim with their wings and their covering over the covenant chest of the LORD.

[19] All of these were written in the hand of the LORD and given to me so that I could understand all the works of the design.

[20] And David said to Solomon his son, "Be strong and courageous, and act. Do not fear or be dismayed, for the LORD, my God, is with you; he will not leave you or forsake you until all the work for the service of the house of the LORD is finished."

[21] And behold, the divisions of the priests and Levites are assigned to every service in the house of God, and they are with you in every work, and every willing person in wisdom for every craft, and the leaders and all the people are for all your words.

---
Notes
- v. 3: "You will not build a house for my name" — the Hebrew uses "לִשְׁמִי" ("for my name") in reference to the temple, a common biblical idiom for the dwelling place of God.
- v. 5: "the throne of the kingdom of the LORD" — the Hebrew is "כִּסֵּא מַלְכוּת יְהוָה," which reflects the divine kingship over Israel.
- v. 14-17: The detailed measurements and weights for the temple furnishings are translated to retain their specificity and function.
- v. 20: "Do not fear or be dismayed" — the Hebrew uses "תִּירָא" and "תֵּחָת," which are standard biblical verbs for fear and discouragement.
- v. 21: "every willing person in wisdom for every craft" — the Hebrew "לְכָל־נָדִיב בַּֽחָכְמָה" is interpreted to reflect both willing volunteers and those skilled in wisdom.
